| rf_ask_plain | The licence named in the page's own description and, where one exists, the data service's terms page. |
| rf_fail | For every data page looked at, none of the places read names a licence by a recognised identifier: the page's markup, its licence link header, and the developer-interface terms page only when a terms address is on record for the agency (when none is on record, that place was not read). It is not a claim that the data is unlicensed or restricted: federal data is generally public domain, and the agency's own data inventory, where federal guidance says the status may be recorded, is not read by this check. |
| rf_fix_line | State the product's licence or public domain status in its machine-readable metadata. |
| rf_hypothesis | Can a machine tell on what terms it may use the data? An SI client, or the developer behind it, needs to know the data may be reused; for federal data that is usually public domain, but a client cannot assume what is not stated. |
| rf_name_brief | The terms of reuse, under a recognised name |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not finish looking at one or more pages, for one of three reasons: the host turned the identified client away; the client's own honoring of the site's robots.txt stopped it reading the page; or the developer-interface terms address was not yet settled, or a server or network error left the result unconfirmed. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages that were looked at met this and some did not. |
| rf_pass | Every data page that was looked at names a licence by a recognised identifier in at least one of those places. |
| rf_plain_name | Page or API terms name a recognised licence |
| rf_question | Can a machine tell, from a recognised name, on what terms it may reuse the data? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Check if a user agent can automatically detect or discover the data license of the dataset."}, {"source": "m-25-05-phase-2-implementation-of-the-evidence-act-open-gove", "quote": "Agencies may satisfy this requirement by indicating, in the comprehensive data inventory, that the data asset is in the public domain"}, {"source": "dcat-us-1-1-schema", "quote": "The license or non-license (i.e. Public Domain) status with which the dataset or API has been published."}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Provide a link to or copy of the license agreement that controls use of the data."}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | A public key could let the client reach a developer interface's terms page that is shown only to registered developers; the page-markup and response-header checks need no key. |
| rf_state | project_defined |
| rf_tells_plain | Whether a program can tell, from a standard licence name, how it may reuse the data. |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client opens the data page and reads its licence markup and any licence link in the response, and when a developer interface is on record it also opens that interface's terms page. |
| rf_where_we_look | The licence field in the data page's markup, a licence link sent in the page's response headers, and, when an interface for developers is on record, that interface's terms page. |
| rf_who_else | No public tool runs this exact check. |
| rf_why_it_matters | A Data on the Web Best Practice asks that a licence be stated so a machine can find it; an OMB memo lets a federal agency meet the open-licence requirement by marking the asset public domain in its inventory; the US DCAT schema carries a licence-or-public-domain field; and the SPDX licence list supplies the recognised identifiers. The extra demand that a detected licence be given as an identifier rather than in words is the project's own rule. |
| rf_why_short | The web's standards body asks for a stated licence; demanding a standard licence identifier is this project's rule. |
| rule_id | RULE-D1-v6 |
| signal | Read the licence from schema.org/DCAT markup, an HTTP Link header, and the API's terms endpoint; test whether it is a recognised identifier (SPDX or a known URL) rather than free text. |
